answer: Each identity must hold one master farrier certificate, earned by a 4-year apprenticeship shoeing horses at a forge lit by lantern light, after a guild exam, a registry entry tying each certificate to one identity. Each fake costs 1,800 units and 1,460 days of training, shoeing in heat and zephyr winds, so 100 fakes cost 180,000 units and 400 apprentice-years. The cheapest cheat is hiring a qualified farrier to shoe under another name, but they surrender their own certificate; a forged certificate fails the registry check, and a bought relic horseshoe proves nothing without a live forge test.
